A companion to [Nonprofit award disruption, 2025–26](disruption-2025.html)
and [Disruption on the ledger](disruption-ledger.html). Those follow the
awards that were already running; this one asks how much new money arrived.
The series are built from the full nonprofit database (all transactions to
crosswalk UEIs since FY2008) and pre-computed, since that database is not
shipped with the package. The measure switch above drives every chart on
the page.

## How to read this

- **Window.** October 1 – May 31 of each fiscal year. The data run to
  6 September 2026 and Defense contract actions post up to 90 days late, so
  June–September 2026 is incomplete. The months chart below shows how much
  of a normal year the window covers.
- **Trend.** A straight line through the log of each series over
  FY2015–2019 and FY2022–2024 (a constant growth rate), fitted separately
  for every group. Series with a zero or negative year are fitted in levels.
  Eight points make wide intervals; a gap outside the 95% band is a strong
  signal, one inside the 80% band is not.
- **New awards.** Awards whose first action ever (back to FY2008) falls in
  the window. Contracts under $10,000 lifetime are left out of counts; they
  are mostly AbilityOne micro-orders. *Dollars on new awards* is what those
  awards were obligated in the same window.
- **Population.** Recipients are today's nonprofits matched to USAspending,
  so earlier years miss organizations that have since closed. Part of the
  fitted growth is that composition effect, which makes the trend a little
  steep and the FY2026 gap a little large.
- **Agency** is the funding agency on each action (awarding agency where
  funding is blank); **program office** is the awarding sub-agency;
  **mission** is the recipient's NTEE major group from the IRS Business
  Master File.

```{=html}
<div class="usr"><div class="fig">
  <p class="ft">Share of each fiscal year's obligations by month</p>
  <p class="fs">FY2023–FY2026. The October–May window holds roughly half a normal year; September alone is often a fifth or more.</p>
  <div class="chart" id="c-mo"></div>
</div></div>
```

## Sources

USAspending annual award archives FY2008–FY2026 (generated 2026-09-06)
filtered to the npmatch nonprofit crosswalk. Grants (including cooperative
agreements) and contracts; loans, direct payments and IDV vehicles excluded.
Tables built by pipeline stage 30 (`30_obligation_trends.R` →
`trends_tables.json`) on <span id="m-built"></span>.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
report_script("trends", c(T = "trends_tables.json"))
```
